why: A dictionary write `d[k] = v` with k = '__proto__' finds no own key and reaches the setter of Object.prototype (ECMA-262 10.1.9 OrdinarySet, B.2.2.1.2): an object or null replaces the prototype, a primitive is ignored, no key is made. own: the parent writes its object only under another key, the candidate's computed literal key makes an own key on every key (unproved; lane B WITNESS on '__proto__'). mark: a primitive written under '__proto__' makes no key, the candidate answers as if it did (unproved; WITNESS on '__proto__'; proved equal before this reading). tally: two writes against one through another name, both skipped on '__proto__' (proved). named: an object under a literal key through a const of literal type (proved). keep untouched. A dynamic key with an object value is refused, rule prototype (escapes proto_write_object.ts, proto_write_null.ts).
